newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-HUBER DEFENDS TITLE IN LEIPZIG.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HUBER DEFENDS TITLE IN LEIPZIG.

text.p: Germany's Anke Huber came from a set and 3-0 down to retain her Leipzig tennis title with a 5-7 6-3 6-1 victory over Iva Majoli of Croatia on Sunday
Majoli, seeded third, looked to have the match sewn up until she had what appeared to be movement problems. Huber, spurred on by the German crowd, took full advantage.

Tears were rolling down Majoli's cheeks at one point but it was not clear if she had suffered an injury or was simply exhausted as she was unable to get anywhere near some blistering passing shots from the fourth-seeded German.
Majoli seemed to recover in the final set but by then Huber had too much momentum.
"This is a great tournament. I'd love to came back next year," a delighted Huber said afterwards.
Huber may have profited from an unexpected rest day on Saturday, when her semifinal opponent Steffi Graf withdrew because of a knee injury just hours before the match.
The loss of the world number one, who may have to rest for three to four weeks, meant Huber went through to the final by default.
Graf's withdrawal meant Huber had been given a helping hand to the title for the second year in a row. She was awarded it last year when fellow finalist Magdalena Maleeva withdrew beacuse of illness.
